Evan / team — quick technical note to complement Marissa's commercial:

Assumptions based on your Q3 usage file (thanks): average request size ~120 tokens, peak concurrency ~220 concurrent streams during peak hour. For a 32-GPU reserved pool using Redwood's default shard placement (A100-class equivalent), conservative throughput estimate is ~310–360 concurrent streams sustained with p95 token latency under 350ms, assuming normal KV cache hit rates.

If you need a tighter p95 (sub-250ms) at peak we recommend:
- Enabling prefix KV caching and per-route micro-batching (no code changes)
- Reserving 4 additional GPUs as warm spare for burst (billed as reserved with a lower burst rate) or enabling our burst capacity bucket for the first 30 days.

I reviewed the SLA addendum: proposed credit is 5% of monthly reserved spend for a single missed target and scales. We can tune the SLA thresholds for p95 and throughput to match your internal SLOs — happy to put numbers next to each customer-critical route.

Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
